newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament rejects cut in aid to cereal farmers.
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament rejects cut in aid to cereal farmers.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday voted against a proposal to cut aid to cereals and oilseeds farmers by 1.3 billion Eecus in order to fund aid for beef producers hit by the mad cow crisis.

European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, arguing that cereals farmers are over-subsidised, proposed to reduce compensation payments for income losses caused by taking farmland out of production.
In a report to the Parliament, German Euro MP Honor Funk said that cereals farmers were not responsible for the mad cow crisis and should not be penalised unfairly.
The Commission was seeking to use the mad cow crisis as an excuse to reduce the cost of cereals payments following a bumper harvest and to pave the way for a fundamental reform, teh report said.

The proposal to cut cereals aid is attached to the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package which is due to be wrapped up by EU farm ministers in Luxembourg between June 23-25. The European Parliament only has an advisory role in the process.
